IN THE  HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CRIMINAL WRIT PETITION NO. 5951 OF 2025
Moshe Shek …..Petitioner
Vs.
The State Of Maharashtra …..Respondent
_____________________________________
Mr.  Niranjan  Mundargi  with  Mr.  Pushkraj  Deshpande  and  Mr.  Rohan
Marathe i/by ALMT Legal for the Petitioner.
Mr. P .P . Chavhan i/by Adv. Komal Punjabi for the Respondent No.1-BMC.
Mr. Ajay Patil APP , for the Respondent-State.
_____________________________________
CORAM  : A. S. GADKARI AND
RANJITSINHA RAJA BHONSALE, JJ.
    DATE  :    22nd DECEMBER, 2025.
P.C.:-
1) By this Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of  India,
the Petitioner is seeking lodgment of crime on the basis of comp laint dated
9th September, 2025, submitted to the Senior Inspector of Police, Nagpada
Police Station, Mumbai of which cognizance has not been taken by the
concerned police Authority .
2) Mr. Mundargi, learned Advocate for the Petitioner submitted
that,  the  Petitioner  had  earlier  filed  WP  No.3009  of 2025  with  similar
prayer however, at the relevant time the complaint with the said Police
Station was not filed on the basis of a representation/complaint subm itted
1/2

ssm                                                                        2                    61-Wp.5951.2025.doc
to  the  Mumbai  Municipal  Corporation  and  therefore  the  Petitioner has
withdrawn the said Petition unconditionally .
2.1) He submitted that, though the said Petition was withdrawn
unconditionally , a separate cause of action now arises from the complaint
dated 9th September, 2025 filed by the Petitioner before the Nagpada P olice
Station, Mumbai-400 008.
3) It is the settled position of law and as has been reiterated by
the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of 
M. Subramaniam  & Anr. Vs. S.
Janaki & Anr., reported in (2020) 16 SCC 728  that, Petition under Article
226 of the Constitution of India for lodgment of crime is not maintainable,
however the Petitioner is having remedy of filing a private complaint before
the jurisdictional Magistrate.
4) In view of the above, Mr. Mundargi, learned Advocate for the
Petitioner seeks leave to withdraw Petition with liberty to f ile a private
complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate, on the basis of his Complaint
dated  9 th September,  2025  submitted  to  the  Nagpada  Police  Station,
Mumbai, as may be permissible in law.
4.1) Leave and liberty granted.
5) Disposed off as withdrawn with aforesaid liberty . 
(RANJITSINHA RAJA BHONSALE J.)   (A.S. GADKARI, J.)
